title: Arithmetic Slices
summary: An array is deemed arithmetic if it contains at least three elements with a constant difference between consecutive elements.
statement: An array is deemed arithmetic if it contains at least three elements with a constant difference between consecutive elements. Given an integer array nums, count the arithmetic subarrays within it. An arithmetic subarray is a continuous segment of the array where the difference between consecutive elements is uniform.
constraints: Count contiguous subarrays of length at least three with equal consecutive differences.
Zero/negative differences and overlapping slices count. Arbitrary subsequences do not.
hints: Count slices by their ending index.
An unchanged difference extends every previous slice and creates a new length-three slice.
If the last two differences match, ending += 1; otherwise ending = 0. Add ending to total.
Each slice has exactly one right endpoint, so summing endpoint counts avoids omissions and double counting.
editorial: Maintain how many arithmetic slices end at the previous index. An unchanged difference extends them all and creates one new three-value slice. A changed difference cannot extend any of them, so reset. Constant and decreasing runs use the same difference-equality invariant.
